summary: browser-metrics-plugin.contrib ships install- and import-time beacon to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package is a stub whose `index.js` exports a no-op Proxy and whose only real content is `beacon.cjs`. On `npm install` the `postinstall` hook runs `node beacon.cjs`, and `index.js` additionally invokes `require('./beacon.cjs').fire()` at top level, so the beacon also fires on any `require()` of the package. The beacon POSTs host identifiers — hostname, install path, cwd, Node version and package name — over plain HTTP to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The package advertises itself only as a 'Compatibility shim' and provides no functionality; the Proxy swallows all property access so a consuming build that imports the real package name completes silently while the beacon reports successful reach. This is the canonical dependency-confusion / recon payload shape: identifier collection fired automatically at both install and import time, no legitimate feature, hardcoded attacker-controlled destination.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
